Look up abstracts for a table of references

Source: R/abstracts.R
fetch_abstracts.Rd

Fills in an `abstract` column by looking each reference up in [OpenAlex](https://openalex.org), a free, open index of scholarly works with an official API. Use it on the results of [scholar_parse_html()], whose results list has titles but no abstracts, or on any data frame with titles (and optionally DOIs).

Usage

fetch_abstracts(
  data,
  title = "title",
  doi = "doi",
  year = "year",
  text = "abstract",
  api_key = Sys.getenv("OPENALEX_API_KEY"),
  min_match = 0.85,
  max_year_diff = 1,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  delay = 0.1,
  fetch = .get_json
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, for example from [scholar_parse_html()] or [bib_to_df()].

title, doi, year

Names of the columns holding the title, DOI and year. Missing columns are skipped.

text

Name of the abstract column to create or fill (default `"abstract"`).

api_key

Your OpenAlex API key (see above). Defaults to the `OPENALEX_API_KEY` environment variable.

min_match

Minimum title similarity (0 to 1) needed to accept a title search result.

max_year_diff

Largest difference in publication year (your `year` vs OpenAlex's) accepted for a title match. The default of 1 allows for online-first dates; raise it (or use `Inf`) for references whose year differs because of re-editions, then check them with `closest_year`.

overwrite

If `FALSE` (default), references that already have an abstract keep it.

delay

Seconds to wait between requests.

fetch

Function used to download JSON; for testing.

Value

`data` with the abstract column filled in, plus: `abstract_source` (the OpenAlex id), `abstract_match` (title similarity, 1 for a DOI match), `abstract_status` (why a reference has no abstract: `"found"`, `"no abstract on file"`, `"title not matched"`, `"year differs"`, `"no results"` or `"lookup failed"`), and `closest_title` / `closest_score` / `closest_year` (the nearest OpenAlex title, for references that were not matched, so you can see whether `min_match` or `max_year_diff` would help).

Details

A reference is looked up by DOI when it has one, otherwise by title. A title search is only accepted when the best match is very similar to your title (see `min_match`) and the publication years agree to within a year; anything less certain is left as `NA` instead of risking the wrong abstract. Many, but not all, works in OpenAlex have an abstract, and coverage is best for recent articles, so expect some `NA`s. Check a few matches by eye using `abstract_match` and `abstract_source`.

OpenAlex now requires an **API key**, which is free: create an account at <https://openalex.org>, then copy the key from <https://openalex.org/settings/api>. A free key allows 100,000 credits a day; a title search costs 10 credits and a DOI lookup 1, so a few thousand references fit in a day. Without a key you get only about 100 credits a day (roughly ten lookups). Pass the key as `api_key`, or save it once with `Sys.setenv(OPENALEX_API_KEY = "your-key")` (or in your `~/.Renviron` file) and it is picked up automatically.

Each title (or DOI) is sent to OpenAlex over the internet, along with your key. Nothing is sent to Google. If OpenAlex says the allowance is used up, the function stops and returns what it has; run it again on that result and it looks up only the references still missing an abstract.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- scholar_parse_html("~/Downloads/scholar_page1.html")
res <- fetch_abstracts(res, api_key = "your-openalex-key")
topic_model(res, k = 4, id = "title")
} # }
